title: 10,000 OpenAI agents solved a million-dollar problem, but the credit is in dispute - TCR 09/09/26
description:
OpenAI said roughly 10,000 autonomous agents resolved the 90-year Navier-Stokes Millennium Problem with a machine-checkable Lean proof, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome Atlas with molecular-effect predictions for roughly 9 billion single-letter substitutions across the reference human genome, free for research, and the Energy Department closed a $1.9 billion loan to restart Iowa's Duane Arnold reactor with Google as the buyer.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-9-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:59 AI agents resolve the Navier-Stokes problem
5:01 DeepMind gives away the AlphaGenome Atlas
7:51 A third nuclear plant restarts for AI compute
10:58 Safety commitments drift in the dark
14:06 A hedge fund runs on AI agents
17:36 Close

This episode covers OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof and the credit fight with NYU and Anthropic mathematicians, DeepMind's petabyte-scale AlphaGenome Atlas, the Duane Arnold nuclear restart and Google's €13 billion Finland buildout, a hash-pinned study finding 67% of frontier safety-commitment changes undisclosed, and a hedge fund running on AI agents at 1% of its old payroll.

On Tuesday, OpenAI said 10,000 agents on an unreleased model resolved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, returning a Lean formalization any researcher can verify, as an NYU mathematician alleged his uncredited work seeded the result and OpenAI denied it. The formal proof can be machine-checked against its stated premises, which drains some weight from the dispute over who arrived first. Google DeepMind gave away the AlphaGenome Atlas, turning rare-variant analysis from a coding job into a web-page lookup, already helping a Broad Institute team pin a non-coding variant to a severe epilepsy case. The Energy Department is reopening Iowa's Duane Arnold reactor on up to $1.9 billion in federal loans with Google as the primary buyer, while Google signed its first non-US nuclear deal in Finland. A hash-pinned corpus traced 710 safety commitments across twelve developers and found 67% of material changes went undisclosed, as a left-right coalition demanded the White House publish its review rules. And a hedge-fund manager rebuilt his firm on AI agents at under 1% of its former payroll, even as aggregate US employment shows no AI-driven job losses and a patent-drafting trial found AI raised work quality without eroding expertise.
